# Confidence Estimation for Error Detection in Text-to-SQL Systems

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#confidence-error)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/download/34699/36854) · AAAI 2025 proceedings; linked arXiv:2501.09527v1 supplies Appendices A-H

**Reading coverage:** All nine proceedings PDF pages and experimental Appendices A-H in the 15-page extended version, including tables and plot captions. Extended Figures 7–10 visually inspected.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Extended manuscript, Appendices A–H](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.09527v1)

## Research question

Detect erroneous SQL and unsupported requests under domain, compositional and answerability shifts.

## Method

Uses token-entropy or sequence-probability scores with thresholding, logistic regression or Gaussian-mixture selection, and compares post-hoc Platt/isotonic calibration. A known portion of shifted data is used for fitting.

## Evaluation

T5, Llama 3 and GPT-based DAIL-SQL are tested on English PAUQ cross-database, template and length splits plus EHRSQL; execution match labels errors.

## What the results support

Rejection often catches unanswerable inputs more readily than wrong SQL for relevant questions. Calibration improves, especially for T5; strong shift can make rejection discard many correct answers.

## Limits and qualifications

Fitting on known shifted examples differs from deployment without labeled target data. The paper uses task-specific risk/coverage and Result EX definitions; its plotted error-detection gains should not be presented as universal conditional-risk guarantees.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Shows why answerability detection and incorrect-generation detection need separate reporting, even when they share a confidence score.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.
